4dd095ae-b6bc-4b66-ba6d-b36459a6feb1.curriculum: University of Canberra does not offer a single generic 'Bachelor of Creative Industries' course of its own. Students enrol in one of its specialisation coded variants, delivered with TAFE Queensland at the Brisbane South Bank campus: Acting and Performance (ARB401), Applied Fashion (ARB402), Contemporary Music Practice (ARB403), Drama and Performance (ARB404), and Visual Arts. Each variant shares a common Core Major in Professional and Creative Industries (24 credit points), including Professional Practice 1 and 2 (Work Integrated Learning), Creative Practice 1 and 2, and Creativity and Culture: Truth and Ideation, but differs in its Specialist Major. The Contemporary Music Practice variant (ARB403), for example, adds a 24 credit point Specialist Major in Contemporary Music Practice covering units such as Synthesis and Sampling, Songwriting and Production, Commercial Music Performance and Music for Media, plus 24 credit points of open electives drawn from TAFE Queensland or UC Bruce units. The degree is 72 credit points, standard 3 years full time.
4dd095ae-b6bc-4b66-ba6d-b36459a6feb1.admission_requirements: Admission is based on an entrance rank, achieved through Year 12 ATAR, a diploma pathway, another Australian qualification, work experience or an overseas qualification, plus an audition or portfolio outcome for most specialisations. For the Contemporary Music Practice variant (ARB403), applicants who meet the minimum entrance rank are required to complete an audition as part of the admission process, at a date and time set out in the offer letter. Alternative entry pathways are also available.
4dd095ae-b6bc-4b66-ba6d-b36459a6feb1.english_requirements: An IELTS Academic score of 6.0 overall, with no band score below 6.0, or equivalent. Confirmed on the Contemporary Music Practice specialisation page (ARB403) and consistent with the figures already stored against this row.

6988099f-0d81-41a9-be84-b6a02f18c132.curriculum: University of Canberra does not offer a single generic 'Bachelor of the Built Environment' course of its own. Students enrol in one of its specialisation coded variants: Architecture (ABB001) or Interior Architecture (ABB002). Each shares a common Core Major in the Built Environment (24 credit points), including BE: Analysis Studio, Heritage Conservation, BE: History and Culture, and Work Integrated Learning Professional Practice units, but differs in its Specialist Major. The Architecture variant (ABB001) adds a 36 credit point Specialist Major in Architecture covering units such as Built Environment Technology 1 to 3, BE: Design Studio, BE: Visual Communication, Architecture: History and Theory 2 and 3, and Architecture Studio 1 and 4, plus 12 credit points of open electives from anywhere in the university. The degree is 72 credit points, standard 3 years full time.
6988099f-0d81-41a9-be84-b6a02f18c132.admission_requirements: Admission to this course is based on an entrance rank, achieved through Year 12 ATAR, another Australian qualification, work experience or an overseas qualification. No assumed knowledge is required and a number of alternative entry pathways and admissions schemes are available. Sourced from the Architecture specialisation page (ABB001).
6988099f-0d81-41a9-be84-b6a02f18c132.english_requirements: An IELTS Academic score of 6.0 overall, with no band score below 6.0, or equivalent. Confirmed on the Architecture specialisation page (ABB001) and consistent with the figures already stored against this row.
